summary: Rabbit Hole is a 2010 American tragedy film directed by John Cameron Mitchell and starring Nicole Kidman, Aaron Eckhart, and Dianne Wiest. Its screenplay by David Lindsay-Abaire adapts his 2006 play of the same name, and Kidman produced through her company, Blossom Films. The plot follows a couple struggling to heal after the death of their young son. The note says the film was critically acclaimed for Kidman's performance but was a box office flop.
one_line: A 2010 American tragedy film directed by John Cameron Mitchell, starring Nicole Kidman as a mother grieving her young son.
key_facts: Rabbit Hole is a 2010 American tragedy film.
Rabbit Hole stars Nicole Kidman, Aaron Eckhart, and Dianne Wiest.
Rabbit Hole was directed by John Cameron Mitchell.
The screenplay of Rabbit Hole is an adaptation by David Lindsay-Abaire of his 2006 play of the same name.
Nicole Kidman produced Rabbit Hole via her company, Blossom Films.
Rabbit Hole premiered at the 2010 Toronto International Film Festival in September 2010.
The plot of Rabbit Hole deals with a couple struggling to heal after the death of their young son.
Rabbit Hole received a limited release in the United States on December 17, 2010.
Rabbit Hole expanded nationwide in the United States on January 14, 2011.
Nicole Kidman was critically acclaimed for her performance as Becca Corbett in Rabbit Hole.
Nicole Kidman received Academy Award, Golden Globe Award, and Screen Actors Guild Award nominations for Best Actress for Rabbit Hole.
Rabbit Hole was a box office flop, grossing only $5.1 million against its $3 million budget.
